body_text:
Euclidean division. For every integer $a$ and every positive
integer $b$, there exist unique integers $q$ and $r$ such that
$a=bq+r$ and $0\leq r<b$. The uniqueness depends on the specified
range for the remainder; without it, infinitely many pairs $(q,r)$
represent the same equation.
